question: to the Commission Yannis Maniatis (S&D), Nikolas Farantouris (S&D), Nikos Papandreou (S&D), Sakis Arnaoutoglou (S&D) Subject:

On 16 August, Türkiye issued two presidential decrees establishing two so-called ‘national marine parks’, one in the area between Fethiye and Kaş excluding the entire marine area around the Kastellorizo archipelago and the other in the marine area between Samothrace and Limnos. These marine parks, which are based on the illegal Turkish doctrine of the ‘Blue Homeland’, do not recognise the legal status of the Greek islands of Kastellorizo, Samothrace and Limnos, as provided for in international law and the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, which is part of the European acquis. The marine parks extend beyond Turkish territorial waters, violating Greek sovereign rights since they include areas of the Greek continental shelf and EEZ, and even territorial waters to which the Greek Aegean and Eastern Mediterranean islands are entitled under UNCLOS. The announcement about the establishment of the two ‘marine parks’ came after Türkiye submitted the relevant maps to the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of UNESCO around this time last year. These along with other new acts of provocation challenge Greece’s sovereign rights in the Aegean and Eastern Mediterranean and constitute a further escalation, effectively nullifying the ‘calm waters’ policy. In view of this: What measures does the Commission intend to take to provide practical support to Greece against Türkiye's unilateral and illegal actions?
